entities.summary:
The Battle of Stamford Bridge was a pivotal event in 1066 that saw the Viking forces of King Harald Hardrada clash with the English army led by King Harold Godwinson. Taking place in the East Riding of Yorkshire, England, on September 25, 1066, this battle marked the end of the Viking invasion of England. The battle's outcome had significant consequences, shaping the course of English history and paving the way for the Norman Conquest of 1066.

The Battle of Stamford Bridge was a decisive victory for the English army, with reports suggesting that over 3,000 Viking soldiers were killed in the fighting. The English army, led by King Harold Godwinson, was able to exploit the Viking army's weaknesses, ultimately leading to their defeat. The battle's outcome had far-reaching consequences, including the rise of the English monarchy and the decline of the Viking influence in England.

The Battle of Stamford Bridge is remembered as a turning point in English history, marking the end of the Viking era and the beginning of a new era of English dominance. The battle's legacy can be seen in the many historical accounts of the event, including the writings of the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle. One of the most striking aspects of the battle's legacy is the fact that it marked the last major Viking invasion of England, a legacy that has endured for centuries.

The battle's significance can be summed up in the words of the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle, which described the battle as a 'great victory' for the English army. This victory marked a new era in English history, one that would be shaped by the English monarchy and the decline of Viking influence in the region.
